READING Time: 25 minutes (13 points) Below is a text with the same story that is told from three different points of view. Read each version and do the following tasks. 1. I followed my son through the door of our house after a long day of work. “Uh, Dad, we have a problem here,” said my son. As I came into the kitchen, I saw that everything that had been on the table was now on the floor! So much for relaxing after work! How did this even happen? * * * 2. When the humans left for the day, I noticed the smell of peanut butter toast in the kitchen. Dogs can’t resist peanut butter. When we smell it, we just have to eat it! So I tugged the tablecloth to knock the toast off the table. Suddenly, the mail, books, and empty cups and plates all fell to the floor. Some cups and plates broke into very little pieces! I gobbled the toast and then hid under the bed. * * * 3. I’m starting to think our house is haunted. When I came home with my dad today, it was like a ghost had thrown everything from the table onto the floor. I wonder if this has anything to do with the toast I left on the table this morning. You will hear the dialogue twice. Now you have 30 seconds to look through the questions. Пауза 30 сек Now we are ready to start. Father: Hey, Anna, do you remember what month it is? Mother: Of course, I do, George! How can I forget our son’s birthday? He will turn 11 years old! Father: Philip will be 11 in just two weeks! Unbelievable! Let’s choose a gift for him while he is at school. Mother: Good idea! He still loves puzzles, doesn’t he? Which puzzle will it be this time? Father: I know that he is dreaming of a 3-D puzzle, some kind of model of a famous building. He’s never had one like that. Can I show you something on my computer? Here’s a great online shop that sells all these puzzles. Mother: Wow! Look at that! Here! The Moscow Kremlin looks great! Father: Actually, Philip told me that he had helped one of his friends make a 3-D puzzle of the Moscow Kremlin. You know – his friend John? Mother: Oh, yes! Well, if he has already done it, let’s choose something else. How about Big Ben in London? Or the White House in Washington, D.C.? Do they have them? Father: I’m sure they do. Here they are. Wait. They each have over 3 thousand pieces and take more than 15 hours to complete. And the pieces are metal. They are not for children. Mother: No, that won’t do. Oh, look! Here’s a pretty Russian church! I think it’s from St. Petersburg. Father: Let’s see. Actually, it’s St. Basil’s Cathedral from Red Square in Moscow. It was built by Ivan the Terrible in the 16th century. Mother: Philip will love it! He loves history! Father: Yes! So, it has one thousand pieces and will take about 10 hours. And the pieces are not metal. Mother: Perfect! How much is it? Father: It’s usually 40 dollars, but now it’s on sale for only 22 dollars. Mother: It’s almost 50% off! Father: 45% to be exact.
